questions.prompt: eps = 0.1, ratio r = 1.25, advantage A = 2. Value of the clipped objective? (two decimals)
eps = 0.2, ratio r = 1.5, advantage A = -2. Value of the clipped objective? (one decimal)
Advantage -1 and ratio 1.5 (eps = 0.2). What happens to the gradient?
options: It is zero because r is outside the clip range
It is active and pushes the ratio back down
It is active and pushes the ratio further up
questions.explanation: For A < 0 the unclipped term is the minimum when r > 1-eps, so the gradient is A*grad r and the optimiser lowers r.

questions.prompt: Samples have ratios 1.3, 0.7, 1.0, 1.1 and advantages 2, -2, 1, 1 (eps = 0.2). What is the clip fraction? (two decimals)
questions.explanation: Sample 1 (A>0, r>1.2) and sample 2 (A<0, r<0.8) are clipped; the others are active: 2 of 4.

questions.prompt: A single sample has ratio 0.8. What is its k3 KL contribution (r-1) - ln r? (four decimals)
Your PPO run's first epoch shows ratios mostly between 0.6 and 1.6, before any update. What is the most likely cause?
options: The advantages are too large, so the ratios are inflated by their size before the first step
The learning rate is too high, so the first epoch already moves the policy a long way
Old log-probs were recorded in a different policy mode (exploration noise, dropout) than the new ones
The clip range is set too small, so the ratios spread out well beyond one before any update
questions.explanation: At epoch 0 the parameters are unchanged, so the ratio must be 1; any spread means the two log-probs are computed inconsistently.
questions.skillLabel: Debug the ratio at epoch zero

questions.prompt: The ratio is computed as new_logp/old_logp with new_logp = -1.2 and old_logp = -1.5. What value does the buggy code give? (two decimals)
Which statement about PPO versus an off-policy method like SAC is correct?
options: PPO needs fresh data from the current policy, while SAC reuses a replay buffer
SAC requires strictly on-policy data, while PPO can use old data
Both discard their data after a single gradient step
PPO reuses a replay buffer indefinitely, while SAC discards old data
questions.explanation: PPO's surrogate and advantages are tied to the collecting policy; SAC is designed to learn from a replay buffer of older policies' data.
questions.skillLabel: Compare on-policy and off-policy data use

questions.prompt: Normalising advantages to zero mean and unit variance per batch mainly helps PPO because it
options: keeps the step size comparable across batches and tasks, so updates do not overshoot
guarantees that the KL divergence stays below eps for every batch of collected data
makes the critic unnecessary by replacing the learned value baseline with batch statistics
changes the sign of the negative advantages so that they become positive in the batch
questions.explanation: The gradient scales with advantage magnitude; normalising decouples the effective step size from reward scale.
